notes: USDC is Circle's real testnet token, not one we deployed.
The deployer is the episode registry's owner and its first validator, and the escrow's oracle and treasury.
BountyEscrow was redeployed on 2026-09-04 to add settleUtility; the first deployment at 0x583A5Cb7CF570F11CC24be7c4eB74F500Dc4B3b5 could not pay out its utility pool and is abandoned.
Kept as the rollback fallback network after the Hedera migration (see "296" below) — not deprecated, not deleted.
USDC is Circle's real Hedera testnet token (HTS 0.0.429274, not a plain ERC-20) — same non-mock principle as the Sepolia deployment.

Deployed via script/deploy-hedera.mjs (raw viem over Hashio), not `forge script` — forge's local EVM (revm) has no implementation of Hedera's HTS precompile (0x167), which BountyEscrow/DatasetRegistry/FederatedRound now call in their own constructors to self-associate with USDC. A real forge script broadcast against these three failed locally with InvalidFEOpcode before sending any transaction; EntityRegistry/AssetRegistry/EpisodeRegistry (which never touch 0x167) deployed fine through forge in the same run. See script/deploy-hedera.mjs's header.

BountyEscrow/DatasetRegistry/FederatedRound each self-associated with USDC in their constructors — confirmed independently via the mirror node (GET /accounts/{id}/tokens?token.id=0.0.429274 for each), not merely assumed from the deploy succeeding.
The deployer is the episode registry's owner and its first validator, and the escrow's oracle and treasury — same convention as Sepolia.
